chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Fayḍ al-Taymī narrated from Ibn Riʾāb, who said:
I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام forbidding narcissus for the fasting person.
So I said, 'May I be your ransom, and why?' He said: 'Because it is the fragrant herb of the non-Arabs.'

key_terms.النَّرْجِسِ: narcissus; a fragrant flower mentioned here as being disapproved for the fasting person
key_terms.لِلصَّائِمِ: for the fasting person; indicating the ruling pertains to one observing sawm

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام forbid narcissus for a fasting person?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam Abu ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام discouraged the fasting person from using narcissus. The stated reason given in the narration is that it is the fragrant herb of the non-Arabs, making the report relevant to the etiquettes and rulings connected to fasting.
